extracted.intended_audience: proposed respondents, interested parties, members of the public, and government agencies participating in USITC investigations (Section 337 and related antidumping/countervailing duty proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Drafting and filing public-interest and other written submissions, requests to participate, and hearing materials in USITC Section 337 and related investigations, following Commission rules on content, format, confidentiality, service, and electronic filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest issues to address
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments should address whether issuance of the relief specifically requested by the complainant would affect the public health and welfare in the United States, competitive conditions in the United States economy, the production of like or directly competitive articles in the United States, or United States consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General invitations to file comments on any public interest issues raised by the complaint or § 210.8(b) filing; written submissions on the public interest must be filed by the deadline (see deadlines entry) and are limited to five pages (inclusive of attachments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest criterion (i): Usage explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: (i) explain how the articles potentially subject to the requested remedial orders are used in the United States;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe typical end-uses, user groups, distribution channels, and contexts in which the subject articles are used by U.S. entities or consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest criterion (ii): Health/safety/welfare concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: (ii) identify any public health, safety, or welfare concerns in the United States relating to the requested remedial orders;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide factual evidence or authoritative sources showing how an exclusion or cease-and-desist order would create or alleviate health, safety, or welfare risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest criterion (iii): Like or directly competitive domestic articles
rubrics_metrics.description: (iii) identify like or directly competitive articles that complainant, its licensees, or third parties make in the United States which could replace the subject articles if they were to be excluded;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific domestic products, manufacturers, or licensees that make functionally equivalent or substitutable articles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest criterion (iv): Replacement capacity and commercial reasonableness
rubrics_metrics.description: (iv) indicate whether complainant, complainant’s licensees, and/or third party suppliers have the capacity to replace the volume of articles potentially subject to the requested exclusion order and/or a cease and desist order within a commercially reasonable time;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address production capacity, lead times, inventory, supply-chain constraints, and commercial feasibility for scaling replacement production.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public-interest criterion (v): Consumer impact
rubrics_metrics.description: (v) explain how the requested remedial orders would impact United States consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss price, availability, product functionality, downstream industries, and any disproportionate impacts on specific consumer groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadlines and page limits for written submissions (Section 337 complaint)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written submissions on the public interest must be filed no later than by close of business, eight calendar days after the date of publication of this notice in the Federal Register. Any written submissions on other issues must also be filed by no later than the close of business, eight calendar days after publication of this notice in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complainant may file replies to any written submissions no later than three calendar days after the date on which any initial submissions were due. No other submissions will be accepted, unless requested by the Commission. Any submissions and replies filed in response to this Notice are limited to five (5) pages in length, inclusive of attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement (EDIS) and docket identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons filing written submissions must file the original document electronically on or before the stated deadlines. Filings must be made through the Commission’s Electronic Document Information System (EDIS, https://edis.usitc.gov). Submissions should refer to the docket number ("Docket No. 3830") in a prominent place on the cover page and/or the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary's Office will accept only electronic filings during this time. No in-person paper-based filings or paper copies of any electronic filings will be accepted until further notice. For help accessing EDIS, contact EDIS3Help@usitc.gov and consult the Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential treatment request procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to submit a document to the Commission in confidence must request confidential treatment. All such requests should be directed to the Secretary to the Commission and must include a full statement of the reasons why the Commission should grant such treatment. See 19 CFR 201.6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documents for which confidential treatment by the Commission is properly sought will be treated accordingly; all information, including confidential business information and documents for which confidential treatment is properly sought, submitted to the Commission may be disclosed and used by the Commission, its employees and Offices, and contract personnel for specified internal purposes, and by U.S. government employees and contract personnel solely for cybersecurity purposes. All nonconfidential written submissions will be available for public inspection at the Office of the Secretary and on EDIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited disclosure of Business Proprietary Information (BPI) under an APO
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to § 207.7(a) of the Commission's rules, the Secretary will make BPI gathered in the final phase of these investigations available to authorized applicants under the Administrative Protective Order (APO), provided that the application is made no later than 21 days prior to the hearing date specified in this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorized applicants must represent interested parties (per 19 U.S.C. 1677(9)) who are parties to the investigations. A party granted access to BPI in the preliminary phase need not reapply. A separate service list will be maintained for parties authorized to receive BPI under the APO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of appearance and public service list
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons wishing to participate in the final phase of these investigations as parties must file an entry of appearance with the Secretary to the Commission, as provided in § 201.11 of the Commission’s rules, no later than 21 days prior to the hearing date specified in this notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A party that filed a notice of appearance during the preliminary phase need not file an additional notice of appearance during this final phase. The Secretary will maintain a public service list containing the names and addresses of all persons, or their representatives, who are parties to the investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certificate of service requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with §§ 201.16(c) and 207.3 of the Commission's rules, each document filed by a party to the investigations must be served on all other parties to the investigations, and a certificate of service must be timely filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary will not accept a document for filing without a certificate of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing participation requests, videoconference, and remote witness procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests to appear at the hearing should be filed in writing with the Secretary on or before the date specified in the notice. Any requests to appear as a witness via videoconference must be included with your request to appear and must include a statement explaining why the witness cannot appear in person; the Chairman may grant such a request for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For these investigations: hearing begins July 18, 2025 at 9:30 a.m.; requests to appear filed by July 14, 2025; requests to appear via videoconference must explain inability to appear in person; requests to appear as remote witness due to illness or a positive COVID-19 test may be submitted by 3 p.m. the business day prior to the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing and hearing submission deadlines and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall file and serve written testimony and presentation slides in connection with their presentation at the hearing by no later than noon on the day before the hearing (example: noon July 17, 2025). Oral testimony and written materials to be submitted at the public hearing are governed by sections 201.6(b)(2), 201.13(f), and 207.24 of the Commission's rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must submit any request to present a portion of their hearing testimony in camera no later than 7 business days prior to the date of the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing and posthearing briefs conformity and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Each party who is an interested party shall submit a prehearing brief to the Commission that conforms with § 207.23 of the Commission's rules; parties shall also file posthearing briefs that conform with § 207.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines cited in the notice: prehearing briefs due July 11, 2025; posthearing briefs due July 25, 2025. Any person who has not entered an appearance as a party may submit a written statement of information pertinent to the subject on or before July 25, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunities to comment on new information and restriction on new factual information
rubrics_metrics.description: On a specified date the Commission will make available to parties all information on which they have not had an opportunity to comment; parties may submit final comments on this information but such final comments must not contain new factual information and must comply with § 207.30.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example schedule in notice: information made available August 13, 2025; final comments due August 15, 2025; final comments must not introduce new factual information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prehearing staff report timing and public/nonpublic access
rubrics_metrics.description: The prehearing staff report in the final phase of the investigations will be placed in the nonpublic record on a specified date, and a public version will be issued thereafter, pursuant to § 207.22 of the Commission’s rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in notice: prehearing staff report placed in nonpublic record on July 3, 2025; public version issued thereafter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope definitions for subject merchandise (example: hexamine)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the investigations, Commerce (and the Commission) define the subject merchandise with detailed technical and compositional criteria (example provided for hexamine: 'hexamine in granular form, with a particle size of 5 millimeters or less, whether stabilized or unstabilized, whether or not blended, mixed, pulverized, or grounded with other products, containing 50 percent or more hexamine by weight').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scope language includes chemical names, CAS numbers, synonyms, formula, and rules for commingling/processing in third countries; scope definitions determine whether imports fall within the investigations and should be carefully quoted and addressed in submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on accepting additional written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional written submissions to the Commission, including requests pursuant to § 201.12 of the Commission's rules, shall not be accepted unless good cause is shown for accepting such submissions, or unless the submission is pursuant to a specific request by a Commissioner or Commission staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not expect the Commission to accept unsolicited late filings and must follow the rule-based exceptions if seeking to submit additional materials.
